mainEntity.name: Can I use a custom AI master prompt for sensitive US business decisions?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Custom prompts can support US-based business planning and marketing, but they should not be treated as a substitute for professional advice on regulated, financial, tax, privacy, employment, or industry-specific matters. The prompt should identify topics requiring qualified review.

Context: Run My AI Business is educational and focuses on practical AI workflows, not individualized professional determinations. A general draft can organize questions or summarize supplied information, but it may omit important context or contain errors.

Key factors:
- The sensitivity and consequences of the task.
- Whether the output affects customers, employees, money, or compliance.
- The currency and authority of the source material.
- Whether a qualified reviewer needs to approve the result.

Practical guidance: Add a rule that the assistant must flag regulated or high-impact topics and stop rather than guess. Use AI to prepare checklists and questions for review, not to make unsupported final decisions.

This boundary keeps educational automation useful without overstating what a prompt can safely decide.
acceptedAnswer.description: Use AI for organization, drafts, and questions, not unsupported final decisions involving regulated, financial, tax, privacy, employment, or other high-impact matters. Instruct the assistant to flag sensitive topics and obtain qualified review before action.
